issues.legal_issue: A High Court hearing a second appeal cannot disturb concurrent factual findings merely by reassessing evidence, questioning its sufficiency, or drawing contrary inferences.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court both found that the plaintiff was in sole possession of the disputed leased properties.
The defendant’s claim based on a will and an alleged allotment failed in the lower courts.

In second appeal, the High Court relied on inferences about the brothers’ interests and doubts about the grant of the leasehold rights, without recording its own factual findings, and reversed the lower courts.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its jurisdiction by reversing the concurrent finding of possession; the Supreme Court restored the trial court’s decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure confines the High Court’s jurisdiction in second appeal. Findings of fact by the courts of fact cannot be displaced merely because the High Court considers the evidence insufficient or draws different inferences; the assessment of the measure and sufficiency of proof lies with those courts. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal to a High Court from a lower appellate court’s decision.
predicates.concurrent_findings_on_possession: The trial court and the first appellate court made the same finding about a party’s possession.
predicates.reversal_based_on_reassessment_or_eviden: The High Court reversed that finding based on its own assessment of evidence, doubts about the evidence, or its view that the evidence was insufficient.

issues.definition: When a second appeal concerns a concurrent finding about possession and the reversal rests on reassessing evidence or its sufficiency, the concurrent factual finding is preserved.

issues.legal_issue: A court may grant an injunction to protect established possession even when the parties’ title to the property remains unresolved.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought a permanent injunction to preserve possession of the disputed leased properties.
The trial court and first appellate court found that the plaintiff was in sole possession.
The defendant’s claims under a will and an alleged allotment failed, while the question of title was left open for determination in appropriate proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The injunction was properly granted to protect the plaintiff’s possession, without deciding the parties’ title.
issues.legal_principle: On the facts of this case, established possession supported an injunction for its protection even though title was left open. The judgment cites no provision or earlier case for this proposition.

rule.if: permanent_injunction_suit and plaintiff_possession_established and defendant_claimed_basis_failed and title_question_left_open

predicates.permanent_injunction_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking a permanent injunction.
predicates.plaintiff_possession_established: The courts found that the plaintiff was in possession of the disputed property.
predicates.defendant_claimed_basis_failed: The defendant’s asserted basis for claiming the property was not proved.
predicates.title_question_left_open: The court left the parties’ title to be decided in another appropriate proceeding.

issues.definition: In a permanent-injunction suit, when the plaintiff’s possession is established, the defendant’s asserted basis fails, and title is left open, an injunction is granted to protect possession.
